question: A sum of ₹7,250 is lent under simple interest at the beginning of a year at a certain rate of interest per annum. After 6 months, a sum of ₹3,625 more is lent under simple interest but at a rate that is twice the former. At the end of the year, ₹335 is earned as interest from both the loans taken together. What was the rate of interest per annum at which the initial ₹7,250 was lent? [Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.]
solution:
**Given:**

Initial Principal (P₁) = ₹7,250

Additional Principal after 6 months (P₂) = ₹3,625

Total Interest (I) at the end of the year = ₹335

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest, I = P × r × t

Where, r = rate of interest per annum, t = time in years

**Calculations:**

Interest from initial loan for 1 year:

I₁ = P₁ × r × 1

Interest from additional loan for 6 months (0.5 years) at twice the rate:

I₂ = P₂ × (2r) × 0.5

Total interest from both loans:

Iₜₒₜₐₗ = I₁ + I₂

₹335 = ₹7,250 × r × 1 + ₹3,625 × (2r) × 0.5

⇒ 335 = 7,250r + 3,625r

⇒ 335 = 10,875r

⇒ r = dfrac{335 × 100}{10,875}

⇒ r = 3.08

**∴ The required rate of interest is 3.08% per annum.**
